title: Bioprinting Cellularized Constructs Using a Tissue-specific Hydrogel Bioink
protocol: Reconstitute tissue-specific ECM digest solutions as previously described for liver.
Store several hundred milliliters of ECM digest solution in aliquots at -80°C.
Dissolve photoinitiator 2-hydroxy-4′-(2-hydroxyethoxy)-2-methylpropiophenone in water at 0.1% w/v.
Store volumes in the range of 50-100 ml shielded from light at 4°C for several months.
Dissolve thiolated HA separately in water-photoinitiator solution to make a 2% w/v solution.
Dissolve thiolated gelatin separately in water-photoinitiator solution to make a 2% w/v solution.
Dissolve PEGDA, the crosslinker, in water-photoinitiator solution to make an 8% w/v solution.
Dissolve PEG 8-Arm alkyne (10 kDa MW) in water-photoinitiator solution to make an 8% w/v solution.

Combine 4 parts 2% thiolated HA, 4 parts 2% thiolated gelatin, 1 part crosslinker 1, and 1 part crosslinker 2 with 8 parts tissue ECM solution and 2 parts hepatocyte culture media (HCM) or 10 parts water as a generic non-tissue-specific hydrogel.
Vortex the resulting mixture on high for 10 seconds to mix prior to use.
Transfer the mixture into a syringe or printer cartridge for extrusion or bioprinting testing and allow it to crosslink spontaneously at 37°C for 30 minutes (stage 1 crosslinking).
For rheological measurements, transfer the mixture into a 35 mm Petri dish and allow it to crosslink for 30 minutes.
Irradiate the stage 1-crosslinked gels with ultraviolet light (365 nm, 18 W/cm2) to initiate secondary crosslinking (stage 2).
Test extrusion characteristics on the laboratory bench with simple extrusion tests using standard syringes and small gauge needle tips (20-30 gauge).
Push the bioink through a standard syringe to achieve smoothly extruded filaments of hydrogel with few or no bumps.
Extrude lines or simple patterns to determine success.
Load bioink preparations into printer cartridges by pipetting them in.
Allow 30 min for the bioink to undergo spontaneous stage 1 crosslinking within the cartridge before bioprinter integration.
Evaluate extrusion compatibility for bioprinting by printing a simple pattern using the bioink.
Print a 7 x 7 mm pattern comprised of parallel lines.
Apply pressure (e.g., 20 kPa pneumatic pressure) while the printhead moves in the X-Y plane at a velocity of approximately 300 mm/min.
Prepare HCM by adding the thawed contents of the HCM supplement component kit to the hepatocyte basal media (HBM) and sterile filtering.
Thaw the supplement components until liquid.
Add ascorbic acid (0.5 ml) to the 500 ml HBM.
Add bovine serum albumin (10 ml) to the mixture.
Add gentamicin sulfate/amphotericin B (0.5 ml) to the mixture.
Add hydrocortisone 21-hemisuccinate (0.5 ml) to the mixture.
Add insulin (0.5 ml) to the mixture.
Add human recombinant epidermal growth factor (0.5 ml) to the mixture.
Add transferring (0.5 ml) to the mixture.
Sterile filter the combined solution through a 0.45 μm or 0.22 μm filter using a bottle-top filter unit or syringe tip filter.
Determine the cell density of primary human hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, and stellate cells by counting on a hemocytometer after thawing according to manufacturers' instructions.
Combine primary human hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, and stellate cells in an 80:10:10 ratio by cell number in HCM media that has been warmed to 37 °C in a conical tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 520 x g at 20 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving behind the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in HCM media to yield a cell suspension containing 1,000 cells per 40 µl media.
Transfer the cell suspension to 96-well format hanging drop plates.
Add approximately 1,000 cells to each well in HCM.
Maintain the plate at 37 °C in 5% CO2 for 3 days during which multicellular spheroids form.
Collect liver spheroids from the hanging drop plate using a pipettor.
Transfer the collected liver spheroids to a sterile 15 ml conical tube.
Prepare a formulation of liver ECM-containing hydrogel bioink, employing 8% PEGDA and 8% 8-Arm PEG alkyne as crosslinkers.
Let the spheroids settle to the bottom of the conical tube for 1-2 minutes.
Remove all media by carefully aspirating or with a pipettor.
Transfer an appropriate volume of freshly prepared hydrogel bioink solution to the conical tube containing the spheroids, generally 10%-25% greater than the volume of the 3-D construct to be printed.
Carefully pipette up and down to resuspend the spheroids in the hydrogel bioink solution.
Transfer the resuspended spheroid-hydrogel mixture to a bioprinter cartridge using a pipettor or serological pipette.
Allow the solution to undergo the first crosslinking stage (thiol-acrylate reaction) for 30 minutes inside the bioprinter cartridge.
